problems.title: Sync scope is client-controlled; handshake can widen access
problems.notes: W2 step 1. resolveSessionScopes is grant ∩ handshake (collection set = grant keys; $in narrowing only; empty grant = nothing visible); $claims grants bound to schema scopes, unresolved binding denied (SCOPE_REQUIRED warning / ScopeRequiredError). Kora providers (toSyncAuthProvider, KoraAuthProvider, TokenAuthProvider, ExternalJwtProvider, MixedAuthProvider) always return a server grant. Remaining hardening for CUSTOM providers that return no scopes: ClientSession.handleHandshake must pass resolveSessionScopes(..., { authenticated: this.auth && !(this.auth instanceof NoAuthProvider) }) and may use onUnresolved:'throw' to answer SCOPE_REQUIRED (session/* owned by W1).

problems.title: Revoked device keeps working via refresh and HTTP routes
problems.notes: W2 step 2. BuiltInAuthRoutes.authenticateAccess() used by every route, requireAuthUser and the sync provider; refresh checks device record and user.

problems.title: OAuth state not bound to initiator or purpose (link CSRF takeover)
problems.notes: W2 step 7. OAuth state bound to purpose/user/client binding (HttpOnly cookie or body); POST /oauth/:p/link/start; device id never from state metadata.

problems.title: Invitations claimable by anyone; cross-org revoke
problems.notes: W2 step 8. listMyInvitations(userId) resolves verified email server-side and strips tokens; accept requires verified email match (checked before consume); OrgStore.revokeInvitation(orgId, id).

problems.title: Client-chosen deviceId not bound to user (lockout attack)
problems.notes: W2 step 3. registerDevice throws DeviceOwnershipError (409) in memory/SQLite/Postgres stores; random default device id; OAuth ignores state device ids.

problems.title: Concurrent refreshes with one token both succeed
problems.notes: W2 step 4. TokenRevocationStore.consume() atomic (SQLite/Postgres INSERT ON CONFLICT); same-instance duplicates get 409 REFRESH_IN_PROGRESS. Postgres contract test passes against PG16 (KORA_PG_TEST_URL).

problems.title: Reset token disclosed without callback; reset does not revoke sessions
problems.notes: W2 steps 2+9. Reset token never disclosed (exposeTokenForDevelopment opt-in, never in production; loud error when no callback, no constructor throw because the repro constructs one); reset/change revoke all earlier credentials; atomic reset-token consume. Repro AUTH-7 opts into allowInMemory for its production case.

problems.title: Sign-out does not stop the access token on HTTP routes
Account enumeration by timing; weak sign-in rate limit
problems.notes: W2 step 9. Dummy-hash KDF for unknown emails; per-account and per-IP limiter keys. Client IP trust is W1 step 7 (SEC-9a).

problems.title: MFA not enforced at issuance; TOTP brute force and replay
problems.notes: W2 step 10. MFA challenge at issuance (mfa_pending token, POST /auth/mfa/verify, amr); TOTP failure backoff persisted; consumeCode in disable/regenerate.

problems.title: Live sync sessions never re-checked after revocation or expiry
problems.notes: Auth side done: AuthContext.expiresAt populated; createKoraAuthServer().onRevoke() and bindSyncServer({ terminateSessions({userId?, deviceId?}) }) emit on device revoke, sign-out, revokeAllForUser. Needs KoraSyncServer.terminateSessions + ClientSession expiry timer (AUTH_EXPIRED, retriable) in packages/server/src/session|server (W1 owner).

problems.title: In-memory revocation store in quickstart; no persistent store ships
problems.notes: W2 step 4. SqliteTokenRevocationStore / PostgresTokenRevocationStore; user stores expose getTokenRevocationStore() used by default; production refuses in-memory stores unless allowInMemory; templates use persistent user stores.

problems.title: Offline users are signed out and their refresh token destroyed
problems.notes: W2 step 6. Only a Kora JSON 401 / 400 invalid_grant clears tokens; request timeout; backoff + Retry-After; Web Locks single refresher; authenticated-offline session (identity from stored credentials) used by createKoraAuthSync, namespaceByAuthUser and AuthBoundKoraProvider; maxOfflineGraceMs lock; clock-rollback guard.

problems.title: Passkey UV, external JWT exp/aud/iss, webhook replay/SSRF, AdminApi authz
problems.notes: W2 step 11. Passkey UV enforced; ExternalJwt exp required + aud/iss (supabase default aud); webhook timestamped signatures + https/public targets + DNS check; AdminApi isAdmin + credential revocation.

problems.title: One retried refresh permanently bans the device from sync
problems.notes: W2 step 3. Device revocation is a cut-off (revokedBefore); reuse revokes the token family.

problems.title: Two tabs refreshing at once sign out every tab
problems.notes: W2 step 6. Web Locks single refresher with storage re-read (in-realm fallback), and the server grace replay covers cross-realm races.

problems.title: Lost rotation response triggers reuse-detection sign-out
problems.notes: W2 step 3. One grace replay within 30s returns the byte-identical successor pair (deterministic jtis, nothing stored); closed once the successor is used.

problems.title: restoreSession treats a 401 from /auth/me as offline
problems.notes: W2 step 6. restoreSession treats a Kora JSON 401 from /auth/me as definitive. Repro written: packages/auth/tests/repro/NEW-AUTH-4.test.ts (fails at beta.12).
